conviction_note: The baseline says the chain is unrecoverable, but the corpus itself carries the number: a 2026-08-17 item states LexinFintech options implied a 10.4% post-earnings move against a 3.1% median over the past eight quarters, with calls leading puts 10:9 - so the market was pricing ~1.7x the baseline's 6.25% anchor and was, if anything, tilted long. I therefore size the move near 10% and take a negative half of it, because the two things the marginal buyer in this capture is long (a new buyback and a maintained dividend) are the two things management already withdrew, and the sector's cleanest print of the week was punished anyway.

findings.finding: LexinFintech suspended its share repurchase programme at the Q1 2026 call - after buying 441k shares at $6.37 in late Aug 2025, 1.79m at $5.87 in September and 1.28m at $4.31 in October per the buyback table on p.174 of the FY2025 20-F - and the long thesis visible across the capture is almost entirely a bet that a new, larger buyback plus a maintained dividend lands with this print ('this will fucking fly like crazy when the new buyback is announced', 'Monday with the new buyback I wouldn't be surprised LX flying 50%').
findings.why_not_priced: The capture shows the option flow with calls leading puts 10:9 into the event and a retail base that has explicitly sized positions on a capital-return announcement, i.e. the price contains a call option on a corporate action that the company's own last call removed. A market pricing 'no buyback, dividend cut' would not have calls over puts and would not have bid the ADR up 2.2% on 2026-08-28 on the heaviest volume of the run-in (4.86m vs a 1.98m 20-day average). The buyback-suspension fact is not in any wire item in this capture - it reaches the corpus only as a shareholder recollection of the Q1 call, and the purchase prices come from page 174 of a 20-F that nobody aggregates.
findings.independence: Same-direction, different corpus file: filings.json shows a Form 4 accepted 2026-08-21T12:27:05Z, ten days before the print and at the all-time low, preceded by 144 notices of intent to sell on 2025-09-19 and 2025-11-26 - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1708259/000119312526360007/xslF345X06/ownership.xml (direction of the Form 4 transaction is not recoverable from the index, so this is corroboration of insider activity only, not of its sign).

findings.finding: Every relevant peer reported in the ten days before LX and the corpus records the reaction function: FinVolution printed a beat on 2026-08-27 and reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of RMB 11.5-12.9bn and still fell more than 15%, while Qifu's call 'read like the fall of an empire' - and the reason is on the record, that China lending volumes fell roughly 40-50% in August after the Juzi platform incident, with banks cutting lending lines and short-term risk rates up 20%, all of which falls in Q3 and none of which is in the June quarter LX is about to report.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/577e46b84b8aa280f5960f5306d50aa466c89561.txt, messages of 2026-08-28T03:42:02Z (FINV call summary, August volumes -40-50%), 2026-08-28T00:35:04Z, 2026-08-29T07:53:00Z, 2026-08-26T15:50:48Z ('the Q2 figures next week should be similar to Q1 since none of the damage occurred until after the quarter was done')
findings.why_not_priced: The corpus shows holders drawing the opposite inference from the same events - FINV's beat is being read as bullish for LX ('$LX flying after hours 7% as a reaction... Major squeeze coming Monday') - when the actual FINV tape says a good print plus reiterated guidance was worth minus fifteen percent in this sector this week. The information content of Monday's release is therefore entirely in the Q3 outlook, and LX is described in its own shareholder base as the operator with 'the needed scale to survive, but just barely'. If the market had priced guidance rather than the quarter, the ADR would not have closed higher on 08-28 on record volume.
findings.independence: WARNING - shares a source with finding 1: both rest on docs/577e46b84b8aa280f5960f5306d50aa466c89561.txt, the single 90-message stocktwits aggregate that is the only substantive body in this capture. Treat them as one source cluster and count the larger residual. The independent corroboration for this one is the run-in in quote.json: -19.2% over 20 days to an all-time low of 1.155 on 08-27 on rising volume, which is the sector shock arriving in the price without any LX-specific disclosure in filings.json since the Q1 6-K of 2026-05-26.

baseline_tension: Cuts against the baseline in magnitude and partly against itself in direction: the run-in is -19% over 20 days to an all-time low on capitulation volume, which is the bear case being paid for already, and the corpus's own counter-evidence is real - JFIN printed badly on 08-27 and fell only 3%, peer Q2 delinquency buckets and Fitch consumer-ABS data improved through the quarter, LX reports last with the least residual surprise, and the stock trades near 0.1x book - so my negative tilt is a positioning call on a withdrawn buyback rather than a claim that the numbers will be bad.
corpus_limits: No option chain from the baseline; the 10.4% implied move I use is a 2026-08-17 snippet inside a social aggregate, i.e. two weeks stale and an 11% decline before the print, and a separate 08-19 message claims '+-20%', so my magnitude anchor has real error bars. Not one filing body was stored, so the 13D/A, the Form 4 and the 20-F are index rows and one quoted table. Everything substantive in this capture comes from a single stocktwits document, which is unverified third-party restatement of company calls I could not read; the FINV and QFIN call content in particular is one shareholder's summary. No document in this capture carried a non-empty tripwire_tells, quote.json stops at 2026-08-28 with no post-print bar, and all four sweeps predate the 2026-08-31T11:09Z release, so this name is clean of look-ahead.
